summary: AstroGuard is an interactive space crew health and countermeasure platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) research. Designed to support autonomous medical operations across ISS, Artemis lunar, and Mars missions, its five-module Mission Control Medical Hub unifies preventive care, real-time telemetry, and emergency triage. Astronauts can track ARED, T2, CEVIS, and neuro-vestibular exercise protocols; monitor eight physiological channels with customizable anomaly thresholds and simulation presets; execute interactive clinical checklists for emergencies like SANS, decompression sickness, and cabin contamination; evaluate neutron and cosmic radiation exposure via CSA CANS and Radi-N2 dosimetry models; and explore an interactive matrix mapping NASA's five spaceflight hazards to active orbital countermeasures.
details:
What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

AstroGuard — Mission Medical Hub is an integrated space-medicine and crew countermeasure platform grounded in official NASA Human Research Program (HRP) and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) research. Designed to support autonomous astronaut health monitoring across Low Earth Orbit (ISS), Artemis lunar transits, and deep-space Mars missions, the platform operates as a centralized five-module hub:

- Countermeasure Exercises: Guides astronauts through daily microgravity workout regimens across Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) strength training, T2 treadmill intervals, CEVIS cycle ergometer sessions, and neuro-vestibular balance and fine-motor spatial drills. It features interactive set adjustments, daily completion quotas, and a built-in protocol countdown timer.

- Vitals Threshold Telemetry: Tracks real-time physiological metrics across key channels—including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), systolic/diastolic blood pressure, core temperature, respiratory rate, arterial oxygen pressure (PaO2), intraocular pressure, and cabin carbon dioxide (CO2). Astronauts can customize upper and lower safety limits, drag live telemetry sliders to test instant anomaly alerts, and trigger simulation presets for nominal baselines, high-exertion EVAs, or cabin hypoxia spikes.

- Clinical Medical Scenarios: Provides interactive, step-by-step emergency triage checklists categorized by severity (Critical, Moderate, Routine). It covers spaceflight contingencies including post-EVA decompression sickness, Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), toxic ammonia leaks, cabin CO2 scrubber malfunctions, and renal stone risk.

- Radiation Dosimetry: Compares radiation exposure across 6-month ISS stays, 3-day Lunar transits, and 3-year Mars architectures. It models autonomous neutron and cosmic ray monitoring using CSA's Canadian Active Neutron Spectrometer (CANS), Radi-N2 bubble detectors, EVARM spacewalk badges, and MOSFET sensors, highlighting that neutron radiation accounts for roughly 30% of total ISS exposure.

- HRP Hazards & Research Matrix: Maps NASA's 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight (Space Radiation, Isolation and Confinement, Distance from Earth, Gravity Fields, and Hostile/Closed Environments) directly to active orbital investigations such as ARCHeR sleep actigraphy, Thigh Cuff and B-Complex SANS trials, CIPHER, Zero T2, and Tempus Pro telemedicine.

Benefits and Intended Impact

- Autonomous Deep-Space Care: On a Mars mission averaging 140 million miles from Earth, communication delays of up to 20 minutes and the impossibility of immediate medical evacuation require crews to diagnose and treat emergencies independently. AstroGuard consolidates preventive countermeasures, live anomaly detection, and clinical triage into a single offline-capable interface.

- Terrestrial Healthcare Spin-offs: Spaceflight induces physiological changes that mirror accelerated aging and sedentary health conditions on Earth. By tracking bone demineralization, cardiovascular deconditioning, vestibular adaptation, and CANS neutron dosimetry, AstroGuard's framework translates directly to earthly applications in osteoporosis management, remote rural telemedicine, cancer radiation therapy, aircrew radiation safety, and nuclear threat detection.

Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used

- Frontend & Web Architecture: Built using HTML5, CSS3, TypeScript, JavaScript, and React 19, bundled with Vite and styled using Tailwind CSS and Lucide Icons (lucide-react).

- Backend & AI Integration: Configured with Node.js, Express, and the Google GenAI SDK (@google/genai) alongside Framer Motion (motion) for smooth interface transitions.

- Prototyping & Computer Vision Environment: Developed alongside a Python rapid-prototyping stack utilizing Python, Streamlit, OpenCV, MediaPipe, NumPy, Pandas, and Plotly for biomechanical pose tracking, neuro-motor dexterity assessment, and telemetry visualization.

- Deployment & Version Control: Managed via Git and GitHub, with a zero-dependency standalone HTML build (index.html / astroguard-demo.html) engineered for instant browser execution on GitHub Pages.

How the Project Is Creative

- Closed-Loop Medical Ecosystem: Rather than treating exercise tracking, vital signs, radiation physics, and emergency medicine as isolated tools, AstroGuard links them into a single closed-loop workflow where a cabin CO2 or EVA exertion spike in the telemetry tab directly corresponds to actionable triage steps in the scenarios module.

- Verifiable Scientific Grounding: Every single exercise card, physiological boundary, radiation detector, and emergency protocol is directly hyperlinked to its primary NASA HRP or CSA scientific source, transforming complex agency documentation into an interactive training simulator.

- Neuro-Vestibular & Dexterity Integration: Alongside standard ARED and T2 hardware protocols, the system incorporates targeted sensorimotor gaze stabilization and fine-motor spatial cube coordination drills to address post-landing manual piloting and gravitational transition risks.

Key Factors Considered by the Team

- The Interconnected Nature of the 5 Spaceflight Hazards: We accounted for how hazards compound one another—such as how a sealed, hostile cabin environment (CO2 buildup) degrades cognitive performance, or how microgravity fluid shifts trigger SANS vision changes.

- Cognitive Load Under Emergency Conditions: In a life-critical contingency like an ammonia leak or post-spacewalk decompression sickness, astronauts cannot afford complex menus. We designed a high-contrast, dark-mode orbital interface using Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono typography with instant color-coded severity badges (emerald, amber, rose) and one-click JSON telemetry export.

- Zero-Latency Offline Reliability: Recognizing that deep-space habitats face bandwidth constraints, we ensured the core application state and interactive presentation deck can run entirely client-side in any standard browser with zero external server dependencies.
